transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-30
- Time: 10:00am PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Liam (NovaPay), Priya (NovaPay), Daniel (NovaPay)

Summary: quick recap of last week's run, dug into throughput numbers, batch distribution, and tail latency. Lots of talk about queueing and concurrency.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - run through last week's benchmarks, samir will walk the tuning changes, then we sync on next steps.
[00:18] Liam (NovaPay): yeah thanks, we'll go over the numbers. priya and daniel are on for infra details.
[00:35] Samir (Redwood SE): ok, so high level - we re-ran with continuous batching enabled and set a soft concurrency target of 8 workers per model shard. result: average throughput improved ~2.4x compared to the single-request baseline for your 512-token prompts.
[01:02] Priya (NovaPay): can you remind me - that 2.4x is with batching and also some quantization changes? we only toggled batching right?
[01:18] Samir (Redwood SE): correct, during this run we only changed batching and queue parameters; quantization was unchanged. continuous batching allowed more packed sequences per kernel call.
[01:36] Daniel (NovaPay): we saw the average up but the 95th and 99th latencies spiked during bursts. 99th hit ~820ms on one run, which is above our 500ms SLO.
[01:55] Maya (Redwood AE): right - that's the thing we wanted to surface. batching helps amortize cost but increases tail under bursty concurrent arrivals unless queueing and concurrency are tuned.
[02:12] Samir (Redwood SE): we looked at batch-size distribution - most batches were between 6-12 sequences, but under spikes you get one big batch that starves the queue and pushes other requests behind it. that produces the tail.
[02:36] Liam (NovaPay): what's your recommended concurrency target then? previous was 4, we upped to 8 for the run.
[02:49] Samir (Redwood SE): in our experiment the sweet spot for median throughput was around concurrency 8-10, but for tail stability we recommended a ceiling of 6 per shard with a shallow queue depth (queue size 40-60ms worth of requests) and a max batch size cap of 10. that keeps batches compact and avoids head-of-line blocking.
[03:18] Priya (NovaPay): when you say queue depth 40-60ms, do you mean a latency-based hold time or number-of-requests?
[03:29] Samir (Redwood SE): latency-based hold window - we let the request sit in the short-lived queue for up to 40ms to allow packing. if none arrive it gets dispatched. that small window gives big packing benefits without long tails.
[03:45] Daniel (NovaPay): we can't easily change our client-side throttling for the next week, we have bursts from payment flows. would software queueing on our side be better?
[03:58] Maya (Redwood AE): two options: client-side rate shaping or server-side short hold windows and concurrency caps. for POC we usually recommend server-side queueing + conservative concurrency to get measurable gains quickly.
[04:14] Liam (NovaPay): ok. what about autoscale? we saw node saturation during the midday run.
[04:23] Samir (Redwood SE): autoscale thresholds are important - you want scale-up at lower CPU/GPU utilization than you'd think to avoid sudden queue growth. we proposed scale-up at 60% GPU utilization with a cool-down of 2 minutes. also allow burst capacity of one extra shard for 5-10 minutes.
[04:46] Priya (NovaPay): can you send the exact yaml for those thresholds?
[04:52] Samir (Redwood SE): yes, i'll share a templated autoscaler config.
[05:00] Maya (Redwood AE): quick notes on cost tradeoffs: reducing concurrency to stabilize tail may increase per-token cost slightly; we calculated cost delta ~+12% at the recommended settings vs your max-thru unconstrained run.
[05:18] Liam (NovaPay): that might be acceptable if we meet latency SLOs. can you show the raw logs so we can validate the spike times?
[05:25] Samir (Redwood SE): yes i exported the raw perf logs. i'll share them. the spreadsheet includes per-request timestamps, batch sizes, and node metrics.
[05:38] Priya (NovaPay): any notes on model variants? we had some runs with a smaller quantized variant - it looked faster but had slightly lower quality on a few prompts.
[05:50] Samir (Redwood SE): right - quantized model reduced token compute time but occasionally produced lower quality on a small set of prompts you flagged. for the pilot we suggested serving the quantized variant for low-risk routes and the FP variant behind a policy for higher-assurance calls.
[06:08] Daniel (NovaPay): is routing by policy something we can do in the private deployment? our infra is a hybrid - some on-prem and some cloud.
[06:18] Maya (Redwood AE): yes, Redwood routing supports per-route model variants, and we can set fallbacks. we'll include a suggested routing table in the docs we share.
[06:28] Liam (NovaPay): good. i'd like to drill into the tail cause; is it always big batches or sometimes GC or spikes in RPC latencies?
[06:38] Samir (Redwood SE): mostly big batch head-of-line blocking and queuing, but there's some correlation with host-level GC on the orchestration side in two of the runs. we flagged both. we'll annotate the logs so you can match host events.
[06:57] Priya (NovaPay): for the A/B we plan to run - what's the recommended traffic multiplier and run time so results are meaningful?
[07:10] Samir (Redwood SE): we asked for 2-3x traffic for 3-4 hours to surface burst behavior; ideally run at your typical peak window. we'll give you the exact test harness.
[07:24] Maya (Redwood AE): ok next steps - we'll share spreadsheet, autoscaler yaml, recommended concurrency/batch matrix, and a short how-to for running the A/B.
[07:37] Liam (NovaPay): timeline?
[07:41] Maya (Redwood AE): maya:deliverables by end of week, samir: tuning matrix by friday, priya and daniel: run A/B next week.
[07:50] Daniel (NovaPay): noted. also we need the security docs for the dedicated run - we might move to private if performance is good.
[08:00] Maya (Redwood AE): i'll include the private deployment security checklist and SOC2/ISO notes in the packet.
[08:10] Priya (NovaPay): one more question - what about queue preemption? can urgent low-latency requests bypass batch queue?
[08:20] Samir (Redwood SE): yes, Redwood supports priority routing: you can add a high-priority queue that bypasses packing windows and goes direct to execution when latency-critical. tradeoff is reduced packing for those requests.
[08:38] Liam (NovaPay): that's useful - we'll flag payments path as high-priority.
[08:45] Maya (Redwood AE): great. any other blockers?
[08:50] Priya (NovaPay): no blockers. just need the files and we start the A/B.
[08:56] Maya (Redwood AE): cool, we'll send everything after. thanks everyone.

Recap & next steps:
- Maya to send benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs.
- Samir to share concurrency/batch-size matrix and autoscaler yaml.
- NovaPay (Priya) to run 2-3x traffic A/B for 3-4 hours and share results.
- Daniel to send cluster utilization dashboards and pod specs.

End of transcript.
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR noise: some product names transcribed inconsistently (VPC/V P C, KV cache as K V cache). Meeting is AE+SE led with customer infra and ML owner present. Action items captured in next_steps and action_items fields.
